title: Che cosa farai?
summary: The future: summer plans, predictions about the match, what happens if it rains, and guessing where someone is right now.
canDo: I can talk about plans and predictions with the futuro semplice.
I can use the common irregular futures: sarò, avrò, andrò, farò, verrò.
I can say what will happen if or when something else happens, and make a guess about the present.

items.back: The futuro semplice. Endings: -ò, -ai, -à, -emo, -ete, -anno. In -are verbs the a turns into e: parlare → parlerò.
items.pt: Like PT falarei, comerei, partirei. Unlike in Brazil, Italians really use it in everyday speech.
Feminine in Italian: la bella estate. PT o verão.

items.note: Andare al mare = to go to the seaside.

items.pt: PT perto de. Il vicino is also "the neighbour".

items.note: Tra and fra mean the same.

items.back: Irregular futures put the same endings on a short stem: essere → sar-, avere → avr-, andare → andr-, fare → far-, venire → verr-.
I will do, I will make

items.pt: PT na sua opinião, pra você.

items.back: After se, quando and appena, Italian uses the future in both halves when both things are still to come: quando arriverà, decideremo.
items.pt: PT uses the future subjunctive: "quando ele chegar", "se chover". Italian has no such tense. Use the plain future (or the present).

items.back: The future also makes a guess about now: sarà a casa = he is probably at home.
items.pt: Same idea as PT "Onde será que ele está?" / "Estará em casa".

items.note: Fa brutto tempo = the weather is bad.

items.pt: PT assim que. Not PT "apenas" (= soltanto).
PT ainda. "Ancora una volta" = mais uma vez.

lessons.title: Quest'estate partirò
lessons.canDo: I can talk about my plans using regular verbs in the future.

intro.scene: June. Sara asks Leo about his summer.

lines.meaning: What will you do this summer?

lines.text: Partirò per la Sicilia fra due settimane. Resterò lì fino a luglio.
lines.meaning: I'll leave for Sicily in two weeks. I'll stay there until July.
How lovely! And where will you sleep?

lines.text: Prenderò una casa vicino al mare con Marco.
lines.meaning: I'll take a house near the sea with Marco.
And Giulia? Will she leave with you?

lines.text: No, lei lavorerà tutta l'estate. Poverina!
lines.meaning: No, she'll work all summer. Poor thing!

notes.title: One set of endings
notes.body: Take the infinitive, drop the final e, add -ò, -ai, -à, -emo, -ete, -anno: prender-ò, partir-ai, dormir-à. The stress falls on the ending, and io and lui carry a written accent: partirò, partirà.

notes.title: -are becomes -er-
notes.body: Verbs in -are change the a to e: lavorare → lavorerò, restare → resterò, parlare → parlerò. Not *lavorarò.

notes.title: 🇧🇷 PT tip: use it
notes.body: In Brazil the simple future ("partirei", "viajarei") sounds bookish and people say "vou partir". In Italy "partirò" is normal speech. Italian has no "vado a partire" for the future. The present also works for fixed plans: domani parto.

exercises.meaning: This summer I will leave for Sicily.

exercises.explain: Verbs in -are: the a becomes e. And lei takes -à.

exercises.prompt: "We will take a house near the sea."
options: Prenderemo una casa vicino al mare.
Prenderanno una casa vicino al mare.
Prenderete una casa vicino al mare.

lessons.title: Sarò, avrò, andrò
lessons.canDo: I can use the most common irregular futures.

intro.scene: Marco is already thinking about Sunday. Giulia is not so sure.

lines.text: Domenica ci sarà la partita. Verrai allo stadio?
lines.meaning: On Sunday there is the match. Will you come to the stadium?

lines.text: Non lo so. Dovrò lavorare fino alle sei.
lines.meaning: I don't know. I'll have to work until six.

lines.text: La partita comincerà alle otto. Avrai tempo!
lines.meaning: The match will start at eight. You'll have time!

lines.text: Va bene, allora verrò. Chi vincerà, secondo te?
lines.meaning: All right, then I'll come. Who will win, in your opinion?

lines.text: Vinceremo noi, naturalmente. Sarà una bella serata.
lines.meaning: We'll win, of course. It'll be a great evening.

lines.text: Vedremo! Se perdiamo, farai tu la cena.
lines.meaning: We'll see! If we lose, you'll make dinner.

notes.title: Short stems, same endings
notes.body: essere → sarò · avere → avrò · andare → andrò · fare → farò · potere → potrò · dovere → dovrò · vedere → vedrò · sapere → saprò. The endings never change.

notes.title: Double r
notes.body: venire → verrò · volere → vorrò · rimanere → rimarrò · bere → berrò. Say the double r clearly.

notes.title: 🇧🇷 PT tip: l'anno prossimo
notes.body: Time words for the future: domani, dopodomani, fra due giorni, la settimana prossima, l'anno prossimo. "Prossimo" goes after the noun more often than in PT: l'anno prossimo, sabato prossimo.

exercises.meaning: Tomorrow I will go to Milan.
On Sunday there will be the match.

exercises.prompt: "Will you come to the stadium?" (to a friend)
exercises.explain: Venire → verr-. Verrà is for lui, lei or formal Lei.

exercises.prompt: Build: "I will have to work until six."
exercises.meaning: I will have to work until six.

exercises.prompt: The future of "potere" for io is:

lessons.title: Se pioverà, resteremo a casa
lessons.canDo: I can say what will happen if or when something happens, and make a guess about now.

intro.scene: Friday evening. Leo and Sara are planning the weekend, and Marco is not answering his phone.

lines.meaning: Shall we go to the sea tomorrow?

lines.text: Se farà bel tempo, sì. Ma se pioverà, resteremo a casa.
lines.meaning: If the weather is nice, yes. But if it rains, we'll stay home.

lines.text: Quando arriverà Marco, decideremo. Ma dov'è? Non risponde.
lines.meaning: When Marco gets here, we'll decide. But where is he? He isn't answering.

lines.text: Sono le nove di sera! Avrà il telefono spento.
lines.meaning: It's nine in the evening! His phone must be off.
As soon as I know something, I'll call you.

notes.title: Future on both sides
notes.body: When both things are still to come, Italian likes the future in both halves: se pioverà, resteremo a casa; quando arriverà, decideremo; appena saprò qualcosa, ti chiamerò. In relaxed speech the present is fine too: se piove, restiamo a casa.

notes.title: A guess about now
notes.body: The future can also mean "probably": sarà al lavoro (he must be at work), avrà il telefono spento (his phone must be off), saranno le nove (it must be about nine).

notes.title: 🇧🇷 PT tip: no "se chover"
notes.body: Portuguese has a special tense here: "se chover", "quando ele chegar", "assim que eu souber". Italian does not. Never invent one: after se and quando use the normal future or the present. And never the congiuntivo: *se piova is wrong.

exercises.meaning: If it rains, we'll stay home.
exercises.explain: After se, the plain future (or the present). Never the infinitive or the congiuntivo.

exercises.prompt: Marco is not answering the phone. "Sarà al lavoro" means:
Build: "As soon as I know something, I'll call you."
exercises.meaning: As soon as I know something, I'll call you.

exercises.prompt: Listen. What will they do if the weather is nice?
exercises.text: Se farà bel tempo, andremo al mare.

exercises.prompt: It is late and Giulia is not here. Make a guess: "She must have a lot of work."
Translate from Portuguese, using the future: "Quando eu chegar, eu te ligo."

lessons.title: Lettura: I progetti di Marco
lessons.canDo: I can read a short text about plans for the future and answer questions about it in Italian.

intro.scene: Marco ha deciso di cambiare vita. Leggi, ascolta e poi rispondi.

sentences.meaning: Next year I'll change my life.

sentences.text: A gennaio lascerò il mio lavoro in banca.
sentences.meaning: In January I'll leave my job at the bank.

sentences.text: Con mio fratello aprirò un piccolo ristorante vicino al mare.
sentences.meaning: With my brother I'll open a small restaurant near the sea.

sentences.text: Lui cucinerà e io starò in sala con i clienti.
sentences.meaning: He'll cook and I'll be in the dining room with the customers.

sentences.text: All'inizio non guadagneremo molto, lo so.
sentences.meaning: At the beginning we won't earn much, I know.
We'll have to work on Sundays too.

sentences.text: Ma saremo liberi e faremo quello che ci piace.
sentences.meaning: But we'll be free and we'll do what we like.

sentences.text: Se tutto andrà bene, fra due anni apriremo un secondo ristorante.
sentences.meaning: If all goes well, in two years we'll open a second restaurant.
You'll come and visit us, won't you?

exercises.prompt: Che cosa faranno fra due anni, se tutto andrà bene?

meme.bottom: Also Marco: "Dovremo lavorare anche la domenica"

lessons.title: Racconto: Il ginocchio della nonna
lessons.canDo: I can follow a short spoken story with predictions and answer questions about it in Italian.

intro.scene: Giulia racconta una domenica al mare. Ascolta: chi aveva ragione sul tempo?

sentences.text: Mia nonna Rosa non guarda mai le previsioni del tempo.
sentences.meaning: My grandmother Rosa never looks at the weather forecast.

sentences.text: Dice che il suo ginocchio sa tutto.
sentences.meaning: She says her knee knows everything.

sentences.text: Sabato mattina mi ha detto: domani pioverà, non andare al mare.
sentences.meaning: On Saturday morning she told me: it will rain tomorrow, don't go to the sea.

sentences.text: Io ho riso e ho risposto: nonna, domani ci sarà il sole!
sentences.meaning: I laughed and answered: grandma, it will be sunny tomorrow!

sentences.text: Anche il telefono diceva: domenica farà caldo e non pioverà.
sentences.meaning: My phone said so too: Sunday will be hot and it won't rain.

sentences.text: Così domenica siamo partiti presto per la spiaggia.
sentences.meaning: So on Sunday we left early for the beach.

sentences.text: A mezzogiorno il cielo è diventato nero.
sentences.meaning: At noon the sky turned black.

sentences.text: Ha cominciato a piovere e siamo tornati a casa tutti bagnati.
sentences.meaning: It started to rain and we went home soaking wet.

sentences.text: La nonna ci aspettava alla porta con un asciugamano.
sentences.meaning: Grandma was waiting for us at the door with a towel.

sentences.text: La prossima volta chiederò al suo ginocchio.
sentences.meaning: Next time I'll ask her knee.

exercises.prompt: Come sa la nonna che tempo farà?
Che cosa ha detto la nonna sabato?
options: Che domenica ci sarà il sole.

exercises.prompt: Che cosa è successo a mezzogiorno?
Che cosa farà Giulia la prossima volta?
